payload.title: AI Builders Daily · 2026-06-11
payload.summary:
**Fable** stole the frame: builders kept posting that bigger models are changing how they work, from overnight coding loops to full video production without touching an editor; **Gemini** briefly went down, then came back, a reminder that the stack is getting more powerful and more fragile at once; product signals were everywhere: **Codex** token usage spiked, **Project Genie** expanded, and **Claude Platform** shipped scheduled deployments plus vault-backed env vars; the sharpest takeaway is practical, not philosophical: start with the strongest model, delegate longer horizons, and only optimize down once the magic is real.

今天最抢眼的还是 **Fable**：一堆 builder 都在晒，模型一变强，工作方式也跟着变了，从通宵跑代码到整支发布视频都让它自己剪，连视频编辑器都没碰；**Gemini** 先宕了一下又恢复，挺直接地提醒人一句，能力在往上冲，脆弱点也没少；产品面也很密：**Codex** token 用量突然拉高，**Project Genie** 扩容，**Claude Platform** 也把定时部署和 vault 环境变量放出来了；最有用的结论不玄，先拿最强模型把事情做通，再回头压成本、换小模型。

sections.headline: **Anthropic**’s Mike Krieger says **Claude Fable 5** changes the workflow, not just the output · **Anthropic** 的 Mike Krieger 说，**Claude Fable 5** 改的不是结果，是整套工作流
sections.body:
Mike Krieger describes **Claude Fable 5** as a model that pushes people out of short prompt-response habits and into longer planning, delegation, and review loops. His main point is that the real jump only shows up after sustained use: better intent understanding, stronger task persistence, more trustworthy multi-step execution, and a workflow that feels closer to managing a teammate than querying a tool. He also says the model is forcing new habits around architectural planning, concurrent sessions, and explicit verification, while still leaving room for faster high-context models for day-to-day questions.

Mike Krieger 把 **Claude Fable 5** 讲得很直白：它带来的变化，不只是答案更强，而是把人从那种一问一答的使用习惯里拽出来，转向更长线的规划、委派和复核。重点不在首日惊艳，而在连续用一段时间后才看清的东西：它更懂意图，能扛住更复杂的任务链，跑多步执行时也更稳，整体感觉更像一个能交活的队友，而不是只会回话的工具。他还提到，这种模型逼着人重练方法论，包括先做架构讨论、同时开多条会话、最后认真验收；但在零碎快问快答上，还是需要更快的高上下文模型配合。

sections.headline: Builders should stop climbing the wrong ladder · 真正想做事的人，别再爬错梯子了
sections.body:
Give yourself permission to build.

The traditional career ladder pushes everyone to become a leader, but I just want to be a builder.

As you climb the ladder at most companies, you’re expected to step away from building and fill your time with product reviews, cross-functional alignment, managing up, and performance calibrations.

I know a lot of builders who spent their best years climbing the wrong ladder.

The good news is that this is finally changing. Companies are rewarding builders and ICs more than ever, and even managers are increasingly expected to do IC work too.

But becoming a good builder takes reps, and it’s hard to put in those reps when you’re in back-to-back meetings all day.

So if you’re a builder at heart, embrace it. You don’t have to give up what you’re good at to be a “leader.”

📌 Watch now: https://t.co/wv2SINll18

给自己一个继续动手做东西的许可。

传统职业阶梯总把所有人往“领导者”那边推，但我只想当个 builder。

在大多数公司里，职位越往上，你越会被期待离开一线建设，把时间塞进产品评审、跨团队对齐、向上管理和绩效校准。

我认识很多 builder，把自己最好的几年花在了爬错梯子上。

好消息是，这件事终于在变。公司比以前更愿意奖励 builder 和 IC，甚至很多 manager 现在也越来越被要求做 IC 工作。

但想成为一个厉害的 builder，靠的是重复练习；如果你整天会议连着会议，这种练习很难攒出来。

所以，如果你骨子里就是个 builder，那就认了它。你不必为了成为“领导者”，把自己最擅长的事丢掉。

📌 现在看： https://t.co/wv2SINll18

sections.headline: Start new AI products with the best model first, then optimize down · 新项目先上最强模型，跑通后再往下压成本
sections.body:
Right from the early days of Gemini, enterprises would get the quality/cost tradeoff wrong. They’d often start with the smallest, cheapest model.

The rule of thumb we gave customers:

Replacing a traditional ML model with an LLM - start small, cos you already know what good looks like.

Building something new - start with the most capable model. Think magically. Figure out what’s actually possible first.

Once they had a high-quality working application, we’d help them move to a smaller model while maintaining quality.

从 **Gemini** 很早期开始，企业就在质量和成本的权衡上经常搞反。他们往往一上来就选最小、最便宜的模型。

我们给客户的经验法则是：

如果是用 LLM 替换传统机器学习模型，那就从小模型开始，因为你本来就知道“好”长什么样。

如果是在做全新的东西，那就先上能力最强的模型。先把想象力打开，先弄清楚到底能做到什么。

等他们把一个高质量、能跑的应用做出来之后，我们再帮他们换到更小的模型，同时尽量把质量守住。

sections.headline: **Box** says **Fable** is a major leap in complex knowledge work · **Box** 评测称 **Fable** 在复杂知识工作上明显跃升
sections.body:
Lots of evidence of huge jumps in capability for Fable across coding (and related) tasks. It’s also a major jump in accuracy and success in complex knowledge work tasks.

In our Box AI Complex Work Eval, we tested the model against Opus 4.8 and saw huge boosts across almost every industry. For our eval we give the Box AI Agent, using Fable, a set of hard real world knowledge work problems that deal with enterprise documents. Then score how the agent performs the tasks.

The main differentiators for Fable vs Opus 4.8 is that it doesn't take shortcuts on complex reasoning, it gets multi-step calculations right, and it's significantly more consistent across runs. We saw the biggest leaps in Media & Entertainment (78% vs 61%), Technology (81% vs 73%), Financial Services (89% vs 83%), and Healthcare (66% vs 60%).

Here are some specific examples:

* Legal M&A due diligence: On a task reviewing NDA terms against a semiconductor company's contracting policy, Fable correctly identified that a joint-ownership clause violates exclusivity requirements while a liability cap is permitted under a Super Cap exception. Fable scored 100% vs Opus's 78%.

* Healthcare: On a clinical radiology error audit across 12 reports, Fable precisely categorized each error by severity grade and correctly concluded no Grade 3 errors existed. Opus prematurely escalated a case to "major error requiring immediate departmental review" when the evidence didn't support it — Fable 63% vs Opus 41%.

* Media & Entertainment: On a genre profitability projection task, Fable correctly recognized that a 20% Argentine tax deduction was already embedded in the source spreadsheet figures and didn't double-apply it. Opus applied it again on top — a compounding error across 4 genre calculations that took its score negative on the task vs Fable's 74%.

* Retail analytics: On a task analyzing high-growth product articles against an investment benchmark, Fable correctly computed each article's growth rate individually and identified that only 2 of 5 exceeded the threshold. Opus confused "high growth relative to average" with "above the benchmark" — scoring 61% vs Fable's 94%.

* Financial Services: On a 5-year debt facility projection, Fable correctly applied interest to opening balances and used the right capex figure. Opus applied interest to the total facility amount and computed tax from the wrong base — two compounding errors. Fable scored 83% vs Opus's 62%.

* Technology: On a SaaS feature valuation requiring computation of a Feature Value Index across multiple regions, Fable applied the formula correctly and got exact values for the markets. Opus got the arithmetic wrong on multiple criteria — Fable scored 100% vs Opus's 74%.

Overall, huge step change in complex analysis, work that requires analytical reasoning, and deep domain understanding. Fable will be available shortly in the Box AI Studio for customers to build agents with.

有很多证据表明，**Fable** 在编程和相关任务上的能力出现了大幅跃升；在复杂知识工作里，准确率和成功率也上了一个台阶。

在我们的 **Box AI Complex Work Eval** 里，我们把这个模型和 **Opus 4.8** 做了对比，几乎所有行业都看到了明显提升。这个评测的做法是：让使用 **Fable** 的 **Box AI Agent** 去处理一组和企业文档有关、真实而复杂的知识工作题目，再给它的完成效果打分。

**Fable** 相比 **Opus 4.8** 的几个核心差异是：它在复杂推理里更少抄近路，多步计算更容易算对，而且多次运行的一致性更好。提升最明显的行业包括媒体与娱乐（78% vs 61%）、科技（81% vs 73%）、金融服务（89% vs 83%）和医疗（66% vs 60%）。

下面是一些具体例子：

* 法务并购尽调：在一项把保密协议条款和某半导体公司的合同政策做比对的任务里，**Fable** 正确识别出联合所有权条款违反独占要求，同时也判断出责任上限可以归入 Super Cap 例外。**Fable** 得分 100%，**Opus** 是 78%。

* 医疗：在一项涵盖 12 份报告的临床放射错误审计任务里，**Fable** 精确按严重等级归类每个错误，并正确得出不存在 Grade 3 错误的结论。**Opus** 则过早把一个案例升级成“需要科室立即复核的重大错误”，但证据并不支持这一点，结果是 **Fable** 63%，**Opus** 41%。

* 媒体与娱乐：在一项类型片盈利预测任务中，**Fable** 正确识别出源表格里已经包含了 20% 的阿根廷税收抵扣，因此没有重复计算；**Opus** 又叠加算了一次，四个类型的计算都被带偏，最终那道题甚至得了负分，而 **Fable** 是 74%。

* 零售分析：在分析高增长产品文章并对照投资基准的任务里，**Fable** 正确逐篇计算增长率，并识别出只有 5 篇中的 2 篇超过阈值；**Opus** 把“相对平均值的高增长”和“超过基准”混在了一起，结果是 61%，而 **Fable** 是 94%。

* 金融服务：在一项 5 年期债务融资预测里，**Fable** 正确把利息算在期初余额上，也用了正确的资本开支数字；**Opus** 则把利息算在总授信额度上，税也按错了基数，两个错误一叠，结果 **Fable** 83%，**Opus** 62%。

* 科技：在一项需要跨多个区域计算 Feature Value Index 的 SaaS 功能估值任务里，**Fable** 正确套用了公式，并算出了各市场的准确值；**Opus** 在多项算术上都出了错，所以 **Fable** 100%，**Opus** 74%。

整体看，这在复杂分析、需要分析性推理的工作、以及深领域理解上，确实是一次明显跃升。**Fable** 很快也会在 **Box AI Studio** 里向客户开放，用来构建 agent。

sections.headline: VC travel satire hits the 2026 circuit grind · 一段把 2026 VC 巡回苦旅写透的讽刺帖
sections.body:
2026 is a BRUTAL grind in VC. You start in Davos, freeze in Aspen, hit Upfront, survive Milken, then it’s straight to Paris for the French Open.  Briefly back in NYC for the Knicks. Then, total blur: SuperReturn in Berlin, Founders Forum in London, then back stateside for the World Cup, back to Paris for Raise AI, Idaho for Sun Valley, quick respite in Mykonos, then the Goldman tech gauntlet, Slush in Finland, NeurIPS in freakin’ Sydney… and *boom*, a productive year of thought leadership and adding value is over, and you’re a wreck.

2026 年的 VC 日子真是又苦又满。先从 **达沃斯** 开场，在 **Aspen** 冻一圈，跑 **Upfront**，熬过 **Milken**，然后直飞 **巴黎** 看法网。中间短暂回 **纽约** 看个 **Knicks**。接下来直接糊成一团：**柏林** 的 **SuperReturn**，**伦敦** 的 **Founders Forum**，再回美国看 **世界杯**，再回 **巴黎** 参加 **Raise AI**，去 **爱达荷** 跑 **Sun Valley**，去 **米科诺斯** 偷个喘息，然后是 **Goldman** 的科技连轴转、**芬兰** 的 **Slush**、还有见鬼的 **悉尼 NeurIPS**……砰，一整年“思想领导力”和“创造价值”就这么过去了，人也废了。

sections.headline: Teams should build agents for each other, not just for themselves · agent 不该只给自己团队做，跨团队才更值钱
sections.body:
People should build agents/skills for their cross-functional teams.

For example, if a design team builds a design agent/skill for the marketing team (trained on all of the brand's guidelines and design patterns), then the marketing team can produce more on-brand assets without having to bug designers every time

But the marketing team couldn't have built this on their own; it takes the designer with their expertise, context, and knowledge

Same thing applies to every pair of teams that work closely with each other, often rely on each other, and complain about each other's limited bandwidth

Building agents for your cross-functional teams ensures each team can be more self-sufficient, and moves us to a direction where teams can be organized by "loops" rather than "functions"

大家应该给跨职能协作团队去做 agents/skills。

比如，设计团队如果给市场团队做一个 design agent/skill，里面喂进去品牌规范和设计模式，那市场团队就能更稳定地产出符合品牌调性的素材，不用每次都去戳设计师。

但这东西市场团队自己做不出来，还是得靠设计师手上的专业判断、上下文和经验。

这套逻辑也适用于所有经常一起干活、互相依赖、又总抱怨对方带宽不够的团队组合。

给跨团队做 agents，能让每个团队更自给自足，也会把组织方式慢慢从按“职能”切，推向按“闭环”切。
